description: Per-sub-slice ablation artifact reporting BEFORE/AFTER admitted-cell predictions for each predictor-refinement sub-slice. Each entry covers the 5 admitted activation cells from the latest sm_86 sweep. The artifact is the load-bearing 'headline moved' evidence per the plan's acceptance criterion: contract closure (witness tests pass) without measurable per-cell prediction change on the corpus is insufficient. When the headline does not move for a cell, the entry records `headline_moved: false` plus a `no_op_classification` from the documented enum, so the absence of movement is honestly attributed to a corpus-shape constraint rather than misclassified as success.
ncu_truth_source: data/local_labels/label_admitted.json (cache_hit_rate_l2_sector_pct field normalized to fraction in [0, 1])

entries.interpretation_summary: The slice-geometry sub-slice was ALREADY active in the baseline sweep at sweep_20260514T165947Z_a1closure_ebe60dd: every baseline bundle carries `cache_model_num_l2_slices=6` (sourced from the older `static_device_card` label). What this round changes is the metadata wiring: source label flips to `device_properties_manifest`, the Maeda HRD second-layer flag activates (the flat-L2-capacity layer-1 conjuncted with the per-slice layer-2), and a `cache_model_geometry_provenance` block lands. Empirical finding: the Maeda HRD second-layer produces ZERO per-cell prediction delta on this 5-cell corpus because every admitted cell's working set fits comfortably within the total L2 capacity (6 MB GA102 L2; largest admitted-cell working set is ~1 MB for silu_fwd timing_shape with 1024 CTAs × 256 threads × 4-byte access width). The flat-L2 layer-1 hit decision is therefore trivially satisfied for every per-launch access; the conjunction with the per-slice layer-2 does not tighten the hit decision the per-slice walker already made. The geomean rel_err is byte-identical pre/post-refinement at 0.3185; per-cell residuals are byte-identical. The honest conclusion: the slice-geometry sub-slice cannot move the headline on the CURRENT 5-cell admitted activation corpus. To produce measurable per-cell improvement, either (a) the corpus must be expanded with synthetic canary cells whose working set exceeds the total L2 capacity (a path the user rejected per the loop-bootstrap DEC-1 adjudication; current scope is `Formal closure`), or (b) the empirical impact must come from the remaining sub-slices (sector edges, write policy, CTA interleave, cross-launch state) — though the per-bias-source analysis suggests CTA interleave and cross-launch state are the most plausible movers for the multi-launch (rmsnorm, softmax) and high-CTA (silu_fwd timing_shape) cells.

The sector-edge accounting sub-slice differs structurally from the slice-geometry sub-slice: the multi-sector expansion loop in tools/hrd_profiler/observation_builder.py::_walk_launch is ALWAYS-ON (no flag to disable). There is no 'with-flag vs without-flag' ablation; both baseline and refreshed sweeps already run the same expansion loop, so per-cell before/after predictions are byte-identical by construction. The empirical content of this entry is the WITNESS-FORMALIZATION outcome: the existing SectorEdgeAccountingTest class in tools/hrd_profiler/test_observation_builder.py was extended with explicit 'Contract cell:' tags tying each test method to the plan's 4 contract cells (aligned-fits / aligned-crosses / sub-32B-fits / sub-32B-crosses) and the 2 internal-consistency invariants (per-op-class-counter sum equals observation count; cold + finite count partitions observations). All 6 tests pass under the protobuf-required environment (uv run --isolated --with protobuf). Empirical finding on the 5-cell admitted activation corpus (layernorm / rmsnorm / silu_correctness / silu_timing / softmax_safe, all bf16_sm80): the activation kernels emit primarily 16-bit-element loads coalesced to 32-byte warp-level transactions whose starting addresses are 32B-aligned by the global memory allocator (cudaMalloc returns 256B-aligned addresses; per-thread loads stride at element width and the warp-level coalesced transaction is 32B-aligned when the per-thread stride divides 32). The sector-edge expansion loop therefore iterates range(first_sector, first_sector + 1) for every access in the trace and produces exactly one observation per access — no double-counting or sector-spanning increment occurs. The honest no_op_classification is 'aligned_access_only_corpus': the corpus consists of aligned, sector-fitted accesses that exercise the aligned-fits and sub-32B-fits contract cells but not the aligned-crosses or sub-32B-crosses cells. To produce measurable per-cell prediction delta from a hypothetical sector-edge fix, the corpus would need cells with sub-32B-aligned starts and access widths that cross 32B boundaries — a path absent from the admitted activation corpus and out of scope for the present formal-closure recovery loop per the loop-bootstrap DEC-1 adjudication. The witness tests themselves cover all 4 contract cells via synthetic single-lane single-instruction traces (test_observation_builder.py lines 327-516), so the formalization is complete even though the production corpus is a no-op.

The write-policy classification sub-slice differs structurally from both AC-4.1 (always-on slice geometry with metadata-only flip) and AC-4.2 (always-on sector-edge expansion with no flag). The `_is_no_write_allocate` filter in workloads/simbench_bw/cache_predictor.py lines 170-187 is ALWAYS-ON in the consumer-side aggregator (`_aggregate_launches` at lines 354-410): every observation tagged with `access_kind == MEMORY_OP_ACCESS_KIND_STORE (=2)` AND `memory_op_class in {MEMORY_OP_CLASS_SHARED (=2), MEMORY_OP_CLASS_CLUSTER_DSMEM (=9)}` is excluded from the hit/miss/cold tally. The ablation `before` value computes the hypothetical predicted_hit_rate WITHOUT the filter (treating no-write-allocate stores as eligible for L2 hit counting); the `after` value matches the always-on filter's output (which is what the refreshed sweep at data/sm_86_predictor_accuracy_recovery/refreshed_sweep_round_3/predictor_bundles/ already records). Fresh-trace gate verified: all 5 admitted-cell traces have populated `memory_op_access_kind` per-access fields (the unspecified_kind_count is 0 for every cell), so the `no_access_kind_in_trace` legacy-no-op classification does NOT apply. Per-cell empirical findings: layernorm timing (98,112 excluded of 1,555,904 obs; -1.44e-3 delta), rmsnorm timing (32,704 excluded of 1,130,304 obs; -8.68e-4 delta), softmax timing (32,704 excluded of 868,160 obs; -1.47e-3 delta) — three reduction-heavy multi-launch activation kernels that write intermediates to shared memory before reducing. silu correctness/timing (0 excluded of 2,048/524,288 obs; byte-identical before/after) — two pointwise kernels operating exclusively on global memory with no shared-memory stores; the filter has no observations to exclude. The 2 silu cells use the new no_op classification `no_no_write_allocate_paths_in_corpus` (added to the AC-3 scanner's `_VALID_NO_OP_CLASSIFICATIONS` enum in this round); this is distinct from `no_access_kind_in_trace` (which would falsely claim legacy traces). The geomean rel_err improvement is small but real: 0.31938 → 0.31854 (delta -8.4e-4 absolute, ~0.27% relative). Headline movement at the geomean level is recorded as `true`. The per-cell direction is correct physically: excluding shared-memory stores REDUCES predicted_hit_rate (those stores never reach L2; the model previously over-counted them as L2 hits), which moves the predictions slightly toward the NCU ground truth (over-prediction is the systematic bias being recovered). The magnitude is small because shared-memory stores are a minority of total accesses (~6-27% of stores; ~6-8% of all observations) for these activation kernels.

entries.interpretation_summary: The CTA-interleave sub-slice is FLAG-GATED (unlike the always-on slice-geometry / sector-edge / write-policy sub-slices): tools/hrd_profiler/observation_builder.py::_round_robin_merge_tb_accesses (lines 301-327) is called only when `cta_interleave_enabled=True` is passed to `_walk_launch`. The ablation directly probes the flag flip by re-walking each cell's `dynamic_trace.pb` under both modes and applying the always-on `_is_no_write_allocate` filter for fair comparison with the existing AC-4.3 entry's after values. Other cache-model parameters match the Round 3 refreshed sweep verbatim: capacity_bytes=6_291_456 (6 MB GA102 L2); num_l2_slices=6; hrd_second_layer_enabled=True. Empirical finding: per-cell `before == after` byte-identical for ALL 5 admitted cells, including the inventory entry's named canonical headline candidate `silu_fwd timing_shape` (1024 CTAs). The honest classification for every cell is `disjoint_cta_working_sets`: the activation kernels distribute work across CTAs along disjoint contiguous slices of input/output tensors (standard CUDA 1-D parallel decomposition), so per-CTA working sets do not share L2 sectors and the round-robin merge produces no cross-CTA reuse the sequential walk would miss. For the multi-launch reduction kernels (rmsnorm 3-launch, softmax 2-launch), per-CTA reduction outputs are disjoint by construction (each CTA reduces its own row); the shared-memory stores that occur during reduction are already excluded by the always-on no-write-allocate filter (AC-4.3) and thus contribute nothing to the L2 hit calculation regardless of interleave mode. The witness tests do PROVE the model captures cross-CTA reuse when it exists: `CtaInterleaveAggregationTest::test_two_ctas_sharing_sectors_under_interleave_reports_cross_cta_reuse` shows interleave hits >> sequential hits on a 2-CTA × 4-shared-sector fixture, and the new `test_multi_cta_shared_sector_hit_rate_improves_by_at_least_10pct` shows ≥10pp absolute hit-rate improvement on a 4-CTA × 10-shared-sector fixture with 8-sector L2 (the synthetic fixtures deliver ≈100% and ≈75% absolute hit-rate margins respectively, well above the plan-required ≥10pp threshold). The production activation corpus simply does not exercise this code path. To produce measurable per-cell CTA-interleave impact on the headline, the admitted-cell corpus would need to include a kernel where CTAs explicitly share L2 sectors (e.g., a tiled GEMM where multiple CTAs read overlapping input tiles, or a stencil kernel where halo regions are shared). The current 5-cell activation corpus is exclusively pointwise / per-row-reduction kernels with disjoint CTA work — out of scope for the present formal-closure recovery loop per the loop-bootstrap DEC-1 adjudication.

entries.interpretation_summary: The cross-launch state carryover sub-slice (added per loop-bootstrap DEC-3) extends the walker with a new `cross_launch_state_carryover` kwarg (Round 7 code change in `tools/hrd_profiler/observation_builder.py`): per-slice (and optional flat-layer) LRU survivors from launch N seed launch N+1's trackers at synthetic timestamps so the next launch starts warm. State is scoped per (device, stream) so cross-stream state does not bleed. The walker extension lands in lockstep with: new `LaunchSurvivingState` dataclass; `_extract_lru_order` + `_seed_tracker_with_survivors` helpers; new `cache_model_cross_launch_state_carryover` bundle field threaded through `cache_predictor.py::predict_cache_hit_rate`; new AC-2 scanner defect `bundle_carryover_provenance_mismatch_single_launch` that fail-closes on bundles claiming carryover=True without multi-launch evidence; new `CrossLaunchStateCarryoverTest` class with 3 contract-cell witnesses (overlapping ≥10pp positive / disjoint ≤1pp negative / default-off back-compat regression). Empirical finding on the 5-cell admitted activation corpus: every committed cell trace has `n_launches=1`. The trace capture isolates one kernel launch per `threadblocks/device_*/stream_*/kernel_*/` directory; the rmsnorm and softmax slugs that the goal-tracker AC-4.5 spec described as multi-launch (3-launch reduce+sum+norm and 2-launch reduce+norm respectively) actually persist only ONE launch each in their `dynamic_trace.pb` artifacts under `workloads/simbench_bw/results/`. The carryover code path therefore has nothing to carry to: every cell starts cold by construction. The honest classification for all 5 cells is `single_launch_corpus` (existing scanner enum value). Per-cell before/after predicted hit rates are byte-identical because each cell has exactly one launch, and a single-launch trace produces identical observations whether the walker is in carryover mode or not (the carryover path branches only at the launch-boundary, which never executes for a 1-launch trace). The witness tests prove the model CAN capture cross-launch reuse when multi-launch traces exist (2-launch overlapping fixture delivers 100% hit rate margin under carryover vs 0% cold-start, well above the plan-required ≥10pp threshold; 2-launch disjoint fixture stays within 1pp delta per the negative-control witness). The production corpus simply does not include a multi-launch trace today. To produce measurable per-cell carryover impact on the headline, the corpus would need cells whose trace capture preserves multiple launches per directory — a producer-side extension out of scope for this loop. The AC-7 residual report's `cross_launch_state_residual` bucket will thus quantify as ZERO contribution on the current corpus: not because carryover doesn't work (the witnesses prove it does), but because the corpus has no multi-launch traces for it to apply to.
